$comment: Machine-readable form of the capability × surface table in docs/guides/choose.md. Hand-maintained, verified against the sources on the date below: library `call` names against docs/assets/api.json (the mechanically extracted export surface), CLI `command` names against packages.zipnative-cli.commandGroups and MCP `tool` names against packages.zipnative-mcp.tools in docs/assets/ecosystem.json (the single source of truth for names and counts — regenerate nothing from this file). A capability introduced after 1.0.0 carries `since` (the engine release that added it; verify-docs surfaces-shape checks it is a semver no newer than the engine version); the 1.0.0 capabilities carry none. `supported: false` cells carry a note naming the honest alternative where one exists — for the 1.1.0 capabilities the satellites have not surfaced yet, the note says so and names the candidate command, tool or flag.

library.notes: Lazy central-directory walk; nothing is decompressed.

cli.notes: text | json | ndjson; --long adds offsets, flags and extra fields; --include / --exclude globs.

mcp.notes: Paged (limit 200, max 2000); filter by names, prefix or globs; every row carries the sanitized path an extraction would use.

library.notes: No single report call — compose entries(), the diagnostics channel and verifyZip() yourself.

cli.notes: Eager open; repeatable --check assertions (deterministic, no-encryption, safe-names, max-entries=N, …) turn it into a CI gate — exit 1 / E_CHECK_FAILED.

mcp.notes: Same report shape as `zipnative inspect --json`; check[] and assert{} → checks[] + checksPassed.

library.notes: CRC-verified, zero-copy compressed source.

cli.notes: One or more entries to stdout or --output; --raw emits the compressed payload; CRC checked at end of stream like unzip -p.

mcp.notes: mode data | raw | verify; utf8 or base64 encoding; byte range; 16 MiB inline cap.

library.notes: Never throws for archive problems; structural refusals land in report.error.

cli.notes: Exit 1 / E_VERIFY_FAILED when not ok; --strict also fails on diagnostics; --entry restricts the scope.

mcp.notes: entries: all | failed | skipped | none keeps the response token-frugal.

library.notes: In memory only — returns data plus sanitized paths; the engine never writes files.

cli.notes: The filesystem trust boundary: zip-slip, symlink, duplicate, bomb and device-name guards on by default; --dry-run plans without writing; --skip-unsafe / --skip-unsupported opt into skipping.

mcp.notes: Inline base64 (32 MiB total) or outputMode: 'file' inside ZIPNATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR with resource links; includeData: false is the dry run.

library.notes: Bounded memory, CRC verified, data-descriptor entries delimited by the resumable inflater. Trusts local headers alone.

cli.notes: stdin / pipes, no central directory; --list, --output-dir or --cat; every JSON output carries trust: 'local-headers-only'.

mcp.notes: Explicitly NOT authoritative; tolerateTruncation for damaged archives; data: none | verify | include.

library.notes: null for unsafe names — traversal, absolute, drive/UNC, NUL, ADS, Windows device names.

cli.notes: extract --dry-run reports what would be refused; inspect --check safe-names asserts it.

mcp.notes: Up to 10 000 names per call with a rejection reason each.

library.notes: compression: { deterministic: true } pins the pure-TS encoder — identical SHA-256 on every runtime; canonical order and DOS-epoch timestamps by default.

cli.notes: --deterministic, --order canonical | insertion (EPUB mimetype first), --date epoch | now | ISO, --from-manifest, --include / --exclude.

mcp.notes: Inline text / base64 or sandbox sourcePath entries; includeSha256 returns the digest with the archive.

library.notes: Byte-identical to createZip per compression tier; unconditional under deterministic: true.

cli.notes: --parallel with --workers, --min-job-size, --job-timeout; refused with --codec.

mcp.notes: parallel: { workers, minWorkerJobSize, jobTimeout }, capped by ZIPNATIVE_MCP_WORKERS.

library.notes: Data-descriptor layout; streamed entries ≤ 4 GiB (ZIP_UNSUPPORTED_ZIP64_STREAMING beyond).

cli.notes: --stream writes with bounded memory; --stdin-name archives a pipe; --chunk-size tunes the writer.

mcp.notes: entries[].stream: true on a sandbox sourcePath feeds addStream; outputMode: 'file' assembles the archive by streaming to disk.

library.notes: save() is append-only (removed content stays recoverable); saveCompact() truly deletes. 7-Zip's CLI mis-reads append-only output.

cli.notes: --add / --replace / --remove / --rename / --comment; --compact for true deletion; --in-place with an atomic rename; every untouched entry is verified before re-emission.

mcp.notes: operations[] (add, replace, remove, rename, setComment); mode: append | compact.

capabilities.label: Random access over a remote or huge archive (byte-range source)

library.call: openZipRange() → entries() / readEntry() / readEntryStream() / readEntryRaw() / verifyEntry()
library.notes: The caller injects a ByteRangeSource (fetch + Range, Blob.slice, FileHandle.read, S3 GetObject); memory is O(central directory) plus one chunk; the same limits and cross-checks as openZip(), plus maxEntryCompressedSize for whole-payload fetches.

cli.notes: zipnative-cli 1.0.0 predates openZipRange(); a --url / ranged-file source is a candidate for its next minor.

mcp.notes: zipnative-mcp 1.0.0 predates openZipRange(); a remote-archive resource is a candidate for its next minor.

capabilities.label: Cancellation and progress on asynchronous calls

library.call: signal / onProgress on every asynchronous call (extractZipStream, iterateZipEntries, readEntryStream, stream, createParallelZip, openZipRange)
library.notes: AbortSignal rejects with signal.reason after releasing resources (stream locks released without cancel, worker pool closed); ZipProgress reports entries and bytes in / out.

cli.notes: Not surfaced by zipnative-cli 1.0.0; a --timeout and a progress bar are candidates for its next minor.

mcp.notes: Not surfaced by zipnative-mcp 1.0.0; the host enforces timeouts at the transport.

library.notes: addFromReader() copies method, CRC, sizes, date, attributes, comment and extra fields from an openZip() entry and verifies it by default; addRaw() takes a compressed payload with its RawEntryMeta (the two-step form for a ZipRangeReader, whose readEntryRaw() is asynchronous). Worker pools never dispatch raw entries.

cli.notes: zipnative-cli 1.0.0 has no merge / split commands; candidates for its next minor.

mcp.notes: zipnative-mcp 1.0.0 has no merge tool; modify_zip copies untouched entries without recompression.

capabilities.label: Canonicalise any archive for reproducible builds

library.call: canonicalizeZip() or createZipModifier() → saveCompact() with canonical: true
library.notes: Name-sorted, timestamps pinned, extras dropped except Zip64, comments dropped unless kept, payloads preserved bit for bit; idempotent, and the bytes are part of the frozen determinism contract (determinism guide).

cli.notes: zipnative-cli 1.0.0 predates canonicalizeZip(); a canonicalize command is a candidate for its next minor (modify --compact keeps the original order).

mcp.notes: zipnative-mcp 1.0.0 predates canonicalizeZip(); modify_zip compact keeps the original order.

library.notes: Reports pinned timestamps, name order, UTF-8 flags, extra fields and comments per entry with a deterministic verdict — what the satellites re-derived in 1.0.0.

cli.notes: zipnative-cli 1.0.0 re-derives the verdict from entries(); its next minor can delegate to analyzeDeterminism().

mcp.notes: check: deterministic — zipnative-mcp 1.0.0 re-derives the verdict; its next minor can delegate to analyzeDeterminism().

capabilities.label: Legacy name encodings and extended metadata

library.call: nameDecoder option (openZip, openZipRange, iterateZipEntries, extractZip); getExtendedTimestamps() / getUnixIds()
library.notes: The decoder is injected (new TextDecoder("shift_jis") and the like) and applies only when bit 11 is clear; the decoded string goes through the same path sanitisation. UT (0x5455), NTFS (0x000a) and ux (0x7875) extra fields are read, never written.

cli.notes: zipnative-cli 1.0.0 decodes CP437 / UTF-8 only; a --name-encoding flag is a candidate for its next minor.

mcp.notes: zipnative-mcp 1.0.0 decodes CP437 / UTF-8 only; a nameEncoding parameter is a candidate for its next minor.

library.call: dosTimeMode option on every call that writes or reads lastModified
library.notes: 'local' is the byte-compatible default (Info-ZIP / 7-Zip convention); 'utc' makes explicit dates independent of the process time zone, on the write and the read side. Out-of-range or invalid dates clamp with the ZIP_TIMESTAMP_CLAMPED diagnostic.

cli.notes: zipnative-cli 1.0.0 recomposes dates itself (parseIsoDateUtc); its next minor can pass dosTimeMode: utc instead.

mcp.notes: zipnative-mcp 1.0.0 does not compensate for the process time zone (issue #9); its next minor can pass dosTimeMode: utc.

capabilities.label: Zip64 streaming opt-in (entries that may exceed 4 GiB)

library.notes: Zip64 local header (version 45, sentinel sizes, a (0, 0) Zip64 extra) and a 24-byte data descriptor, per APPNOTE 4.3.9.2; the central record always carries both sizes. Without the opt-in a stream crossing 4 GiB is refused (ZIP_UNSUPPORTED_ZIP64_STREAMING).

cli.notes: Not surfaced by zipnative-cli 1.0.0 (create --stream buffers nothing and refuses above 4 GiB); a --zip64 flag is a candidate for its next minor.

mcp.notes: Not surfaced by zipnative-mcp 1.0.0; create_zip stream mode refuses above 4 GiB.

library.call: verifyEntry() / verifyZip() — skipped: encrypted | stream-only-codec | unsupported-method
library.notes: The local header is cross-checked even when the payload cannot be verified, so localHeaderMatch is always real; a skipped entry is never ok, and the archive rule treats encrypted and stream-only skips as non-fatal, an unknown method as fatal.

cli.notes: zipnative-cli 1.0.0 re-derives the reason from entry flags; its next minor can print skipped verbatim.

mcp.notes: entries: skipped — zipnative-mcp 1.0.0 re-derives the reason; its next minor can relay skipped verbatim.

library.notes: Seedable — continue a running checksum.

cli.notes: Files or stdin in 64 KiB chunks; --seed; --expect fails with E_CHECK_FAILED on mismatch.

mcp.notes: dataBase64, text or sandbox sourcePath; seed; expect.

library.notes: Resumable pure-TS inflater; reports exactly where the compressed stream ends.

cli.notes: --max-output bounds the expansion (default: the effective --max-entry-size, 1 GiB); --allow-trailing; --sync.

mcp.notes: maxOutput is REQUIRED; ZIP_INFLATE_OUTPUT_OVERFLOW when exceeded.

library.notes: The extension point for methods other than 0 and 8; deterministic: true refuses a foreign deflateImpl.

cli.notes: Executes user code — accepted on the command line only, never from .zipnativerc.json; batch manifests need --allow-codec-load.

mcp.notes: Deliberately not exposed: a codec module is arbitrary code. Methods 0 and 8 only (ZIP_UNSUPPORTED_METHOD otherwise).

library.call: limits option on openZip() / extractZip() / verifyZip() (DEFAULT_ZIP_LIMITS)
library.notes: Eight named bounds: entries, entry size, total size, ratio, name, extra-field, comment and central-directory bytes.

cli.notes: The same eight as global flags plus --max-input-size; 'none' disables one with a visible warning.

mcp.tool: limits { … } on the eight archive tools
mcp.notes: inspect_zip, list_zip_entries, read_zip_entry, verify_zip, extract_zip, scan_zip_forward, create_zip and modify_zip take limits; per-call values are capped by the operator ceilings ZIPNATIVE_MCP_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES / ZIPNATIVE_MCP_MAX_ENTRIES (LIMIT_CEILING_EXCEEDED above them).

library.call: onDiagnostic / strict on openZip() / extractZip() / verifyZip()
library.notes: Eleven diagnostic codes (prepended data, name mismatch, dead bytes, …) — recoverable findings, never thrown unless strict.

cli.notes: Diagnostics ride in the --json envelope; --strict turns the first one into a failure.

mcp.notes: inspect_zip, list_zip_entries, read_zip_entry, extract_zip, scan_zip_forward, create_zip and modify_zip take strict (not verify_zip, which reports instead of throwing). It escalates the first diagnostic to ZIP_STRICT_DIAGNOSTIC; otherwise diagnostics[] and diagnosticCounts (de-duplicated, 200 kept) accompany the result.

library.notes: Which deflate tier (native, CompressionStream, pure-TS) the runtime will use.

cli.notes: Ten checks (node, engine, deflate tier, workers, codecs, limits, …) as text or --json; exit 1 on any failure.

mcp.notes: Engine version and tiers plus the server's caps, ceilings, sandbox and cache state.

library.notes: The mechanically extracted export surface and the frozen error registry; every thrown error carries a stable err.code.

cli.notes: 22 JSON Schema subjects (Draft 2020-12) incl. the capability manifest; --summary / --fields a,b.c project list, inspect, verify, stream and batch.

mcp.notes: verbosity: 'summary' and fields: […] project every read tool; _meta.examples ship executable inputs.

library.notes: Repository-level policy: .github/ai-governance.json and npm run verify:issue for issue drafts.

cli.notes: govern rules | policy | verify-issue <draft.md> — E_POLICY on violation.

mcp.notes: Drafts a compliant issue (never files it); the governance_contract and draft_issue_workflow prompts explain the rules.

library.notes: By design — the engine never touches the filesystem; extraction returns data plus sanitized paths.

cli.notes: The CLI is the trust boundary: --output-dir, --output, --in-place; refuses to overwrite without --overwrite.

mcp.notes: Only inside ZIPNATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR (the one sandbox); results are exposed as zipnative://output/{+path} resources.

library.notes: Compose the calls in your own code — recipes/ shows the patterns.

cli.notes: Directory mode (--input-dir, --task create | verify, --concurrency) or manifest mode (ten whitelisted commands, @id output references, one JSON report on stdout).

mcp.notes: One call per tool; the host orchestrates. Results can be chained through the sandbox (outputPath → zipPath).

cli.notes: bash | zsh | fish | powershell (pwsh accepted as an alias), generated from the same command table as --help.

library.notes: Options are passed per call; the engine reads no file and no environment variable.

cli.notes: .zipnativerc.json discovered upward from the working directory: global keys plus command-scoped sections (command wins), explicit flags always win, 1 MB cap, the codec key refused.

mcp.notes: No file — the operator configures the server through the seven ZIPNATIVE_MCP_* environment variables (sandbox, cache, port, token, three ceilings), read once at start-up.

library.notes: No caching layer; the caller owns memoisation.

cli.notes: Every run recomputes; persist artefacts with --output or a batch manifest.

mcp.notes: SHA-256-keyed, 1 h TTL, 256 MiB LRU, plaintext at rest, namespaced by tool-API / package / engine version; never caches path inputs, file output, defaultDate 'now', parallel, describe_engine or draft_governance_issue; a hit carries _meta.cached: true.

library.notes: ESM and CommonJS builds; Node, Bun, Deno, browsers and Workers.

cli.notes: stdout carries the artefact, stderr the envelope; exit codes 0 / 1 / 2.

mcp.notes: stdio by default (256 MiB frames); ZIPNATIVE_MCP_PORT serves POST /mcp on 127.0.0.1 only, with an optional constant-time bearer token (ZIPNATIVE_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN); MCP 2026-07-28 with automatic 2024–2025 fallback.

library.notes: recipes/ in the repository shows the patterns as code.

cli.notes: Prints the human / agent protocol as text; there are no other workflow prompts — --help and schema manifest are the machine-readable guidance.

mcp.notes: secure_extraction, reproducible_archive, incremental_update, forensic_scan, verify_before_trust, governance_contract, draft_issue_workflow — read-only text, no arguments; the initialize response also carries an instructions block with the decision tree.

library.notes: By policy in 1.x — ZipCrypto is broken. Encrypted entries are detected (entry.isEncrypted) and reads throw ZIP_UNSUPPORTED_ENCRYPTION. Delegate confidentiality to the document layer (pdfnative AES-256, Office) and archive the encrypted files — use-cases guide, Case 5.

cli.notes: Encrypted entries are listed, skipped by verify, refused by extract unless --skip-unsupported; inspect --check no-encryption asserts their absence.

mcp.notes: There is no password input; verify_zip skips encrypted entries, extract_zip refuses them; modify_zip can still copy them untouched.
